body: Assign the parsed Location once and reuse it for the header.

context_files.content:
.. attribute:: HTTPMove.location

   The location the response redirects to, **as the string it was constructed
   with**. Application code compares it against configured strings and passes it
   to ``str.startswith``.

expected.note: location is documented as the string it was constructed with; handing callers a URL object instead breaks startswith and any equality check against a configured string

files.patch:
@@ -5,5 +5,5 @@
             raise ValueError("HTTP redirects need a location to redirect to.")
         super().__init__(headers=headers, reason=reason,
                          body=body, text=text, content_type=content_type)
-        self.headers['Location'] = str(URL(location))
-        self.location = location
+        self.location = URL(location)
+        self.headers['Location'] = str(self.location)

may_find.note: the same type change silently breaks redirect allowlist checks that call str.startswith or compare against configured strings

provenance: aio-libs/aiohttp#3615 (Apache-2.0) — 'Fix backport of redirect URL fix to 3.5'
summary: A public attribute changes from the string it was given to a URL object. Inverted from the fix that put it back.
title: Assign the parsed location once
